title: Double `/`: IEEE
description: `/` on doubles is IEEE 754: `x / 0` is ±inf, `0 / 0` is NaN, `±inf / ±inf` is NaN. No setting changes it. With the `IEEE` candidate, only the four `±inf / ±inf` rows differ, as for DuckDB (duckdb-R15-double-arith).
reference: `divide` with `on_division_by_zero: ERROR` when omitted; `IEEE`, `NULL`, `LIMIT` when asked. `±inf / ±inf` is a domain issue (#257).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: The same section at tag py-2.1.0.

provenance.notes: `Expr.truediv`'s notes say zero division follows IEEE-754: `0/0` is an invalid operation and returns NaN, `n/0` on finite operands is ±infinity. The note is not tied to a float type, and the user guide says `Float32` and `Float64` both follow IEEE 754, so `Float32` division behaves the same (and `±inf / ±inf` is NaN, IEEE's invalid operation). Settles the `Float32` rows and `on_domain_error` (NaN for `0/0` and `±inf / ±inf`) at docs level; the probes cover `Float64`.
